name: NG exhaustion chain Phase-2 P-O-X forensic reopening

supersedes_disposition_only.prior_phrase: P,O,X candidate killed by held-week reversal
supersedes_disposition_only.note: The underlying historical and held observations are preserved. Only the automatic kill/disposition is superseded.

held_20260329.interpretation: The negative held mean is a falsification flag but is not an unusually extreme realization relative to the historical week distribution or the exact same-week shift null. It is insufficient by itself to retire the mechanism.

held_loss_structure.note: Removing one observation does not restore a positive held mean; the reversal is distributed across several cases.

current_vs_latest_predecessor_polarity.interpretation: The held reversal is concentrated in the X-to-same-polarity-current branch. The X-to-opposite-polarity-current branch remained nonnegative in every held instance. Both branches were positive in aggregate across the 54-week base, so this is a conditional/regime question rather than proof that one branch is universally invalid.

path_shape_from_entry_plus5.interpretation: On the held week the two polarity-resolution branches diverged progressively after +10 seconds rather than differing only at the final +60 mark.

successor_before_fixed_plus60_exit.interpretation: A new exhaustion before the fixed +60 exit is not by itself a universal invalidation. The successor's polarity transition interacts strongly with the current-vs-latest branch. This points toward dynamic re-origin/exit semantics rather than a blind fixed-horizon hold. Successor information may be used only when it becomes causally observable, not as an entry feature.

current_mechanism_hypothesis: P-O-X is a branching transition precursor, not a single fixed-horizon state. The latest X state resolves differently depending on the current exhaustion polarity and subsequent re-origin behavior. The held week exposed this branch structure; it did not establish that P-O-X is absent.
next_tests: Reconstruct the P-O-X branches instance-by-instance across all 54 weeks and all six OOT eras using only causally available state at each decision point.
Test current-vs-latest polarity relation as a pre-entry branch because it is known at current t0 and was already permitted in the Phase-2 candidate family.
Test successor-exhaustion onset/polarity as a dynamic exit or state-transition event only when it becomes observable; do not leak it into entry selection.
Determine whether the same-polarity branch has a stable pre-entry discriminator in predecessor timing/state geometry or whether it is genuinely regime-dependent.
Keep P-O-X active until a documented multi-block/mechanistic retirement standard is met. Do not retire it solely because one held fold has a negative mean.

retirement_requires: or repeated independent out-of-time failure after mechanism decomposition
or a predeclared falsifier showing the mechanism is indistinguishable from null across relevant blocks
